Two-person approval ([rbac.approval]). A call on the approval list made
without an approval fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION and leaves a pending
request; once a different user with the approve right approves it, the

Audit trail: who called what, when, and whether it was allowed. Persisted

Backup operations: shipping point-in-time copies OFF the cluster to an

Distinct from snapshots (same pool, lost with the machine) and from WAN DR
(a replica, where a delete replicates). After the first full image, a
backup of a thin volume is incremental: only blocks changed since the last
backup to the same target are shipped.

ImportBackups rebuilds backup records from the manifests on a target, for
a controller that lost its database or a cluster restoring another's.

post.summary: The journals and kernel messages the controller does not hold.
post.description:
ListControllerLogs above is the controller's own ring buffer, and almost
nothing that breaks DRBD appears in it: a promoter that could not start its
target, a resource that will not connect, a kernel that refused the module,
an LVM pool with no space left. Those are on the nodes, and until now the
only way to read them was for a person to ssh in.

The collectors are a fixed table, named and read-only. This is deliberately
not a command channel: a request names collectors, never a command line, so
an unknown name is reported back and nothing is run. See
pkg/controller/diagnostics.go for the table and what each one reads.

get.summary:
Operational notifications: a replica degraded, a resource's Primary moved,
a node stopped answering. ListEvents serves the controller's bounded
in-memory history — enough to see what just happened, not an archive. The
durable record of who did what is ListAuditEvents.

Only events newer than this id. Lets a client resume where it left off
instead of re-reading the whole buffer.

get.summary:
WatchEvents streams notifications as they happen, so an operator (or the
web UI, or a script) can react without polling. Over REST this is a
newline-delimited JSON stream; `curl -N .../v1/events/watch` works.
get.description:
A watcher that cannot keep up loses events rather than blocking the
controller. Event.id is monotonic across the whole stream, so a gap in it
is how a client detects that it fell behind.

parameters.name: sinceId
parameters.description:
Replay retained events newer than this id before streaming live ones, so a
reconnecting client does not miss what happened while it was away. 0 skips
the replay and starts from now.

post.summary: Gateway operations

Self-healing (see docs/user-guide.md "Self-healing"). MoveReplica adds
the new replica and removes the old one once the new one is UpToDate.
PlanRebalance proposes moves from the fullest node; apply runs them one
at a time. MarkNodeLost removes the replicas of a node that will not
return; RestoreNode cleans what a returned node holds of resources it is
no longer part of and lets it take replicas again.
Caps an NFS export directory with an ext4 project quota (gateways
created from this version on); size 0 removes the cap.

SMB gateway (workgroup edition): a standalone Samba server per resource,
its users and shares kept on the gateway's state volume.

post.summary:
Cluster inspection: deterministic checks of everything around the alerts —
replicas stuck mid-handshake, alerts that reach no channel, node clocks,
disks and addresses, pool growth, late backups, Self-HA readiness,
certificate expiry, leftovers. RunInspection runs one now and waits for
the report; it changes nothing on the cluster. A run already in progress
is not overlapped: the call fails instead.

GetInspection returns one stored report; id "latest" (or empty) is the

The controller's own log output, from an in-memory ring buffer. Deliberately
not persisted: this is for watching what a running controller is doing, and
a controller that has moved has nothing useful to say about its old node.

post.summary:
Storage tiering: put an SSD/NVMe device in front of one node's LVM pool
with lvmcache. The cache serves the whole pool, and defaults to
writethrough because a writeback cache holds acknowledged writes that no
other node has yet.

ConvertPoolToThin rebuilds one node's LVM pool as a thin pool, in place.
Thick pools cannot hold a snapshot history: each snapshot reserves a fixed
COW area whether anything changes or not.

get.summary:
Notification channels: where alerts are delivered. These live in the
controller database rather than in controller.toml so they can be changed
from the UI while the controller runs — reconfiguring alerting by editing a
file and restarting means a deliberate window with no alerting at all.
get.description:
A channel has a kind, because a chat service does not accept an arbitrary
JSON document: Feishu, Slack, WeCom and DingTalk each define their own
message envelope and reject anything else, and Feishu, WeCom and DingTalk
do it inside an HTTP 200.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: SaveNotifyChannelRequest creates a channel or replaces one by name.

post.summary:
TestNotifyChannel delivers one synthetic message to a single channel and
reports what the far end actually said, including a rejection returned
inside a 200. It does not go through the event bus, so it neither pages the
other channels nor appears in the event history.
Pool operations

resource's connections over one link at a time.

post.summary: Resource operations

Brings every participant's copy of a resource's DRBD config back into
agreement, tiebreakers and diskless clients included, and applies it.

RepairWanProxy reconciles a WAN resource's replication tunnels with what
the controller currently believes its nodes are: it re-provisions the legs
that should exist and removes instances left behind by a node that was
renumbered or removed. Safe to run on a healthy resource — it converges.

Orders where drbd-reactor starts an HA resource (preferred-nodes). A
preference, not a fence; DRBD quorum is what prevents split brain.

Labels on a resource: the keys in labels are set, then the keys in remove
are deleted. Integrations mark what they run on a resource this way, e.g.
haify.libvirt/domain=<guest>.

PopulateVolume copies a source block device (an LVM/ZFS snapshot, or another
resource's backing volume) into an ALREADY-CREATED, still-empty DRBD
resource. Unlike RestoreSnapshot — which merges a snapshot back into its own
origin in place — this fills a *different*, new volume, which is what CSI
restore-from-snapshot and volume cloning need.
post.description:
The copy is written to the target's DRBD device (not its backing LV) on a
node that holds a replica, so DRBD replicates it to every peer for free.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: resource / volume_id identify the freshly created, still-empty target.

parameters.name: lost
parameters.description:
lost removes the replica of a node that is gone for good: nothing is run
on it, only the survivors' configs change. Refused while the node answers
or any survivor is still connected to it.

post.summary:
Renames a resource that nothing else refers to by name: offline (not
Primary anywhere), with no HA config, gateway, schedule, backups or
snapshots, not WAN-replicated or encrypted. Its data, node ids and port
are kept. The Proxmox plugin uses it to reassign disks and make templates.
Resource snapshots: every volume on every diskful replica, taken with
I/O suspended across them, so a rollback restores all replicas together
and resyncs nothing. Backing snapshots are "<backing>_snap_<name>".

Controller self-HA operations: make the controller itself highly
available on its own DRBD + drbd-reactor machinery.
Snapshot schedule operations (cron-driven snapshots + GFS retention)

Freezing a schedule keeps it snapshotting but stops all pruning, and locks
every scheduled snapshot of the resource until the freeze ends. The
write-anomaly detector freezes one when it fires. A freeze is only ever
extended by Freeze; Unfreeze ends it early.
Storage upkeep: trimming, disks, and long-running storage jobs.

Snapshot operations. Volume identifiers are "<pool>/<lv>" paths, so the
REST bindings need the two-segment pattern {volume=*/*}; a plain
{volume} never matches a value containing a slash. The single-segment
binding is kept for backward compatibility.

REST bindings need the two-segment pattern {volume=*/*}; a plain
{volume} never matches a value containing a slash. The single-segment

get.summary:
Listing ZFS pools was the one RPC in the ZFS pool CRUD triple with no HTTP
binding, so it was reachable over gRPC but absent from the REST API and

post.summary: ZFS operations

drNode.title: registered node that will hold the remote copy

drEndpoint.title: public address the primary site dials

egressAddress.title: optional source address for the primary site

HaifyControllerAddDRBody.description:
AddDRRequest attaches an asynchronous off-site replica to a resource that is
already running, turning a LAN cluster into the two-site shape in place.

device.description: Block device on that node to spend entirely on cache, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1.

mode.description:
"writethrough" (the default when empty) or "writeback". writeback
acknowledges a write once it is on the SSD, so losing that one SSD loses
every write it had not yet destaged, recoverable only from a replica that
happens to hold them.

ignoreFreeSpace.description:
ignore_free_space adds the replica although the node's pool has less free
space than the volume, which the sync writes in full. Without it that is
refused: a full thin pool fails the sync's writes and drops the new disk.

allowUnreachable.description:
allow_unreachable adds the replica while a minority of the resource's
members do not answer; they get the new config when they are back.

HaifyControllerAddReplicaBody.description:
AddReplicaRequest adds a diskful local replica to a running resource. On a
two-site resource the new node also gets its own WAN leg to the DR: DRBD 9 is
a full mesh, and a replica the DR cannot reach ends replication the moment it
is promoted.

HaifyControllerAdjustResourceProfileBody.description:
AdjustResourceProfileRequest brings every member into line with its profile:
DRBD options applied, missing replicas added. Replicas beyond the profile's
count are reported, never removed.

HaifyControllerAdoptResourceBody.description:
AdoptResourceRequest imports an already-existing (foreign) DRBD resource into
Haify management by recording its metadata in the Haify database. It never
creates or modifies the actual DRBD resource or its data. Every field except
name is optional and auto-discovered from the live .res on a node when
omitted; a provided value overrides discovery.

HaifyControllerAttachDisklessClientBody.description:
AttachDisklessClient adds a node to a resource as a diskless data client: it
stores no local replica but connects over DRBD and can be promoted Primary to
read/write the volume over the network. Distinct from a quorum tiebreaker,
which is never promoted. Idempotent.

node.description: node is the primary-site node to promote; empty takes the first.

waitSeconds.description:
wait_seconds bounds how long this call waits for the resync before it
reports progress and returns; 0 does not wait.

HaifyControllerDRFailbackBody.description:
DRFailbackRequest returns a WAN resource from its DR node to the primary site
after a DR failover. Run it again until phase is "done": it rejoins the
primary site (discarding what those nodes wrote after they were cut off),
waits for them to resync from the DR, then moves the Primary role back.

node.description: node reads the target; empty tries the registered nodes in turn.

asOf.description:
as_of (RFC3339) imports the target as it was at that time: the object
versions current then, before any later overwrite or delete. Restores of
what it imports read those versions too. S3 targets with versioning only.

ocfAgents.title: optional OCF agents appended to promoter start[]

startItems.description:
start_items, when non-empty, defines the promoter start[] list verbatim and
in order (systemd units and OCF agents interleaved). The legacy fields
2/3/5/6 above are then used only for provisioning side effects (mount unit
generation, VIP service-ip precondition) and NOT for start[] ordering.

sourceDevice.description:
source_device is the block device to copy FROM, on `node`: an LVM snapshot
(/dev/<vg>/<snap>), a ZFS zvol, or another resource's backing volume.

node.description:
node must hold a diskful replica of `resource` AND have source_device
locally; the copy runs entirely on that node.

dryRun.description:
DryRun reports what would change without touching anything. Worth using
first: repair restarts replication tunnels.

ignoreFreeSpace.description:
ignore_free_space grows the volume although a replica's pool has less free
space than the growth. The added area is resynced onto every replica;
without this a pool that cannot hold it refuses the resize, because a full
thin pool fails the writes and drops the disk.

sizeBytes.description:
size_bytes grows the device to exactly this many bytes; size_gb is then
ignored.

resource.description:
resource is the resource to restore INTO; empty restores into the resource
the backup was taken from. It must exist, be large enough, and not be in
use.

HaifyControllerRunBackupScheduleBody.description:
RunBackupScheduleRequest runs a schedule now, retention included, and waits
for it.

enable.description:
enable=true is strict: WAN (protocol A / async) resources are REFUSED,
because two Primaries over an async link corrupts data, and a failure on
any node fails the call.

enable=false is idempotent: it is the caller's cleanup path, so an unknown
resource or a node that rejects the command is tolerated — but the
effective state is verified afterwards and an error is returned if any
reachable node is still dual-primary.

nodes.description:
nodes limits an enable to these participants — a live migration's source
and target, the two ends of the only connection that will carry two
Primaries. Empty enables it on every participant. Disabling always covers
every participant.

nodes.title: in order; empty removes the preference

policy.title: start-only (drbd-reactor 1.9+) or always; empty = drbd-reactor's default

replicationAddress.description:
replication_address moves DRBD traffic to a separate network; empty keeps
the node's current choice (none = the management address).

moves.description:
moves renumbers several nodes together, instead of node/address — what a
DHCP server handing every node a new lease needs. One at a time cannot
work then: each node's resources are rewritten through peers still known
only by their dead addresses.

HaifyControllerSetNodeAddressBody.description:
SetNodeAddressRequest renumbers a registered node: the controller reaches it
at the new address, checks it is the same machine, and rewrites every place
the old address was recorded — the node registry, /etc/hosts on the nodes,
and the DRBD config of each resource the node takes part in.

HaifyControllerSetNodeLabelsBody.description:
SetNodeLabels sets or merges key=value labels on a node. When replace is
true the node's labels are replaced wholesale; otherwise the given labels are
merged in (a label with an empty value deletes that key).

quorumGuarded.description:
quorum_guarded requests a SAFE hard-failover promote: the controller tries
a normal (non-forced) promote first and only escalates to `drbdadm primary
--force` if the target node currently holds DRBD quorum (majority). If the
node lacks quorum the promote is REFUSED (forcing without quorum could
split-brain). When set, `force` is ignored. Used by the CSI node plugin so
a Pod rescheduled after a hard node failure promotes the survivor iff it is
safe to do so.

labels.description: Set or replace these keys; a key with an empty value is removed.

HaifyControllerSetResourceLabelsBody.description:
SetDualPrimary toggles DRBD's allow-two-primaries for a resource. It exists
for the live-migration hand-off in the Proxmox VE storage plugin, where the
source and target hypervisor both hold the disk open for a moment.

The toggle is applied at RUNTIME only (drbdadm net-options) and never written
into the .res file, so a reboot or `drbdadm adjust` restores single-primary
on its own.

HaifyControllerSetResourceProfileBody.description:
SetResourceProfileRequest makes a resource a member of a profile (applying
its DRBD options), or takes it out with an empty profile.

HaifyControllerSetResourceProfileOptions.description:
SetResourceProfileOptionsRequest records DRBD options on a profile and
applies them to every member.

HaifyControllerSetTiebreakerBody.description:
SetTiebreakerRequest moves a resource's diskless quorum tiebreaker to
another node. An empty node removes the tiebreaker without adding one.

drEndpoint.description:
dr_endpoint is the DR site's address the primary dials: an IP or a host
name, without a port (the WAN port is the resource's own).

egressAddress.description: egress_address pins the source address the primary dials from.

clearEgress.description: clear_egress lets the routing table choose the source again.

skipReachabilityCheck.description:
skip_reachability_check saves and provisions without checking that the DR
endpoint answers — for a DR site whose firewall is not open yet. Without
it, an endpoint that does not answer is refused and the old one restored.

HaifyControllerSetWanEndpointBody.description:
SetWanEndpointRequest changes where a WAN resource's primary site reaches its
DR site, and rebuilds the tunnels on it. An empty field keeps its value.

options.description:
DRBD options as "section/key" -> value (e.g. "net/max-buffers" -> "8000",
"on-no-quorum" -> "suspend-io"). Keys without a section default to the
resource-level "options" section.

node.description:
node is the node to verify from and, with resync, whose data wins. Empty
takes the Primary, else the first diskful node.

waitSeconds.description:
wait_seconds bounds how long this call waits for the verify to finish;
0 does not wait.

HaifyControllerVerifyResourceBody.description:
VerifyResourceRequest compares a resource's replicas block by block (DRBD
online verify) from one node against each of its connected peers. Run it
again while phase is "running" to follow it; with resync it instead copies
the source's data over every block marked out of sync, which makes the
copies identical and clears the marks.

user.description: user is the S3 access key id, or the SMB/WebDAV username.

secret.description:
secret is the S3 secret access key, or the SMB/WebDAV password. It is
write-only: it is never returned by any RPC. Clients are expected to read
it from an environment variable or a file rather than a command-line flag.

secretObscured.description: secret_obscured says secret is already in rclone's obscured form.

lockMode.description:
lock_mode turns on S3 Object Lock for every object written: "governance"
or "compliance"; empty for none. The bucket must have Object Lock (and so
versioning) enabled, and rclone 1.74 or later must be on the nodes.

lockDays.description: lock_days is how long every backup stays locked at the least.

fullEveryDays.description:
full_every_days is how long an incremental chain grows on a locked
target before the next backup is full (default 7). Every backup of a
chain is locked until chain start + full_every_days + lock_days, so no
link expires before a backup built on it.

mode.description:
The mode actually applied, so a caller that sent nothing learns it got
writethrough rather than assuming.

nodes.description: Discovered/recorded metadata, echoed back for the caller to display.

mountPoint.title: where the Primary mounts the volume

adminUser.title: the account whose password was generated

credentialsFile.title: the password, root-only, on the volume

version.title: engine version the nodes agreed on

connection.title: how a client reaches it through the service IP

request.title: the call's arguments as JSON, secrets masked

client.title: caller address, forwarded client IP when proxied

user.title: empty when RBAC is off: no identity exists

node.description:
Node that served the call. The controller relocates, so a trail spanning a
failover is otherwise ambiguous about where each entry came from.

state.description: state is running | completed | failed. Only completed is restorable.

kind.description:
kind is full or incremental. An incremental restores only together with
every backup down to the full one it is built on.

parent.description: parent is the backup an incremental is built on.

schedule.description:
schedule is the backup schedule (resource@target) that took it; empty for
a backup taken by hand. A schedule's retention deletes only its own.

lockMode.description:
lock_mode and retain_until (RFC3339) are the Object Lock its objects
carry; until then it cannot be deleted, by haify or by anyone using haify's
credentials.

readAt.description:
read_at (RFC3339) is the time its objects are read as of, for a backup
imported with as_of.

lastBackup.description: last_backup is the id the last run produced; last_error why it did not.

v1BackupScheduleInfo.description:
BackupScheduleInfo is a cron-driven backup of one resource to one target.
Retention is GFS over the completed backups it made, and never breaks an
incremental chain: a kept backup keeps everything down to its full one.

description.description: description is a rendered one-line summary for display.

v1BackupTargetInfo.description:
BackupTargetInfo describes a backup repository. The secret is intentionally
absent: a credential readable back out of the API leaks through every client
that ever renders it.

ranges.description:
ranges is the object listing the byte ranges an incremental image holds;
empty for a full image.

changedBytes.description: changed_bytes is how much of the volume an incremental image carries.

nodes.description:
Nodes to read. Empty means every registered node, which is what a caller
investigating a cluster-wide symptom wants and is why it is the default.

collectors.description:
Collector names. Empty means all of them. An unrecognised name is returned
in unknown_collectors and runs nothing — a typo must not silently collect
less than the caller asked for.

sinceMinutes.description:
How far back to read, for the collectors that take a window (journals).
0 takes the server's default.

maxLines.description:
Per collector, per node. 0 takes the server's default. A cap is not a
nicety here: dmesg on a node that has been up for a year is megabytes, and
this response is read by an assistant with a context window.

availableCollectors.description:
Every collector this controller knows, so a caller that asked for all of
them can tell which ones it got and a caller that mistyped one can see the
list without a second call.

fields.description: Structured zap fields, rendered as strings so the UI needs no type table.

volumes.description:
Volumes rebuilt on this node; each is resyncing in full from its peers
when the call returns.

password.description:
The generated password, returned only by the call that generated it.
Empty when the volume already held the app's data (data_reused).

node.description:
node optionally pins which replica is snapshotted and read. Empty prefers
an UpToDate Secondary.

full.description: full skips the incremental path even when a base is available.

implementation.title: iSCSI implementation: lio (default; tgt and iet are refused)

token.description: The user's token. Returned once and never stored in clear.

sizeGb.title: single-volume shorthand; ignored when `volumes` is set

pool.title: single-volume shorthand; ignored when `volumes` is set

volumes.description:
volumes lists one or more DRBD volumes to create atomically (volume 0..N).
When empty, a single volume is created from size_gb/pool for back-compat.

wan.description:
WAN replication (opt-in add-on). Absent/false ⇒ LAN, behaves exactly as
before. `wan` is the master switch; without it the dr_* fields are rejected.
See docs/design/wan-replication.md.

route this resource over the internet via a per-resource haify-proxy pair

drNode.title: the DR-site node (must be a registered node); WAN only

drEndpoint.title: the DR site's public WAN address the primary dials; WAN only

wanPort.title: WAN mTLS port (default a random >3000 per resource); WAN only

wanEgressAddress.description:
wan_egress_address optionally pins the source address the primary's proxy
binds before dialing the DR site, so replication leaves over a chosen
interface (e.g. a leased line) and reaches the DR firewall from a
predictable source IP. Empty lets the primary's routing table decide.

replicas.description:
replicas requests auto-placement: when `nodes` is empty the controller
picks this many nodes (most free space in the target pool first). Ignored
when `nodes` is set. 0 means "not auto-placing" unless nodes is also empty,
in which case the controller defaults to 2.

replicasOnDifferent.title:
replicas_on_different names node-label keys (e.g. "rack"); during
auto-placement each replica is put in a distinct value of every listed
label, so a single fault domain never holds two replicas. Only nodes
carrying the labels participate. Empty = capacity-only. Ignored when `nodes`
is set. (Wire-compatible successor of the earlier singular string field.)

replicasOnSame.description:
replicas_on_same names node-label keys whose value must be IDENTICAL across
all replicas (e.g. keep every copy in one zone). Composable with
replicas_on_different. Ignored when `nodes` is set.

doNotPlaceWith.description:
do_not_place_with names other resources; auto-placement will not put a
replica on any node already holding a replica of them (cross-resource
anti-affinity). Ignored when `nodes` is set.

encrypt.description:
encrypt puts a LUKS2 container between DRBD and the backing LVM/ZFS volume
on every replica, so the pool disks hold ciphertext. This is encryption AT
REST ONLY: DRBD sits ABOVE the crypt layer, so replication traffic between
nodes is the same plaintext it always was. Chosen once, at creation: there
is no in-place conversion, and asking for one on a resource that already
exists is refused rather than half-applied.

sizeBytes.description:
size_bytes, for the single-volume shorthand, makes the device exactly
this many bytes (rounded up to a 512-byte sector) instead of size_gb
whole GiB; size_gb may then be 0. PVE's online Move Disk needs it.

shareName.description: The first share, over the whole data volume; defaults to the resource name.

lockDays.description:
lock_days locks every snapshot the schedule takes for that many days: no
retention, full pool or API call deletes it before then. Unset keeps the
current schedule's lock; it can be raised at any time, lowered only once
nothing is locked.

compression.description:
compression is the pool's compression algorithm (on, off, lz4, zstd,
zstd-1..19, gzip, gzip-1..9, lzjb, zle), set on its root dataset so every
volume inherits it. Empty keeps OpenZFS's default, which is on (lz4) from
2.2.

dedup.description:
dedup turns on deduplication for the pool. It costs RAM for the dedup
table on every write; only worth it for data known to repeat.

phase.description:
phase is where the failback stands: "resyncing" (run again to finish) or
"done".

node.title: node that keeps running the standalone controller

resourcesMoved.description: resources_moved lists the DRBD resources whose Primary was moved off the node.

vip.title: virtual IP for the controller (CIDR, required)

pool.title: storage pool backing the metadata resource

port.title: DRBD port for the metadata resource (default 7999)

handoffLog.title: node-local log path of the handoff script

id.description:
Monotonic across the controller's whole event stream, starting at 1. A
watcher whose ids skip a value knows it fell behind and lost events.

status.description:
"firing" when a condition starts, "resolved" when it clears, "info" for
one-shot events that do neither. Pairing these is how a receiver avoids
treating a recovery as a new problem.

resource.title: empty for events not scoped to a resource

node.title: empty for events not scoped to a node

details.description:
Type-specific fields: disk_state / repl_state for degrade events,
from / to for failover events.

v1Event.description:
Event is one operational notification. The same shape is delivered to
Webhook receivers as JSON, so a receiver written against one works against
the other.

v1GFSRetention.description:
GFSRetention is a grandfather-father-son retention policy: how many
snapshots to keep per time bucket. Zero disables a bucket.

primaryNode.title: empty when the resource is Primary nowhere

serviceState.title: systemctl is-active of the unit there

nodes.title: the nodes its promoter runs on

thin.description:
thin: the pool is over-provisioned, so the size is what fits without
overcommitting rather than a hard limit.

v1GetResourceProfileMaxSizeResponse.description:
GetResourceProfileMaxSizeResponse is the largest volume a new member could
get now, and the nodes it would land on.

activeNode.title: node currently running the controller (DRBD Primary)

ocfAgents.title: OCF agents appended after the services

startItems.title: the explicit start list, when one was given

v1HaOutsideService.description:
HaOutsideService is a systemd unit outside the chain that has processes
using the resource's mount on the node running the chain. It holds the
unmount up on a failover, or keeps writing to a mount that is gone.

activeNode.description: active_node is the Haify node running the chain; empty when none is.

outsideSessions.description:
Login sessions (and their processes) using the resource's mount on the
active node; not services, so counted rather than listed.

kind.description:
kind is what the unit is in the chain: promote, mount, service_ip, nfs,
iscsi, nvmeof, smb, database, vm, haify, target or service.

label.description:
label names the unit's job for a person: the mount path, the service IP,
the export or LUN, or the unit's own description.

description.description:
description is the unit file's own Description=, not the
"drbd-reactor controlled ..." one drbd-reactor puts over it.

since.description:
since is when the unit last became active (RFC 3339); empty while it is
not active.

restarts.description: restarts is systemd's NRestarts: automatic restarts since it was started.

subState.description: sub_state is systemd's SubState: running, exited, mounted, dead, ...

mainPid.description: main_pid is the service's main process, 0 when it has none.

reasons.description: reasons says, briefly, what would stop a takeover there.

diskState.description: disk_state is the node's local DRBD disk state of the resource.

v1HaStandby.description:
HaStandby is one node that holds an enabled copy of the promoter but is not
running the chain, and whether it could take the chain over.

v1HaStartItem.description:
HaStartItem is one entry in the promoter start[] list. systemd/mount units and
OCF resource agents are PEERS: the list is a single ordered sequence and each
item is exactly one of the fields below. This is what lets a correct stack be
expressed (e.g. portblock -> Filesystem -> IPaddr2 -> nfsserver -> exportfs ->
portunblock) instead of forcing all OCF agents after all systemd units.

skipped.description:
skipped maps a backup id, or a manifest path when it could not be read,
to why it was not imported.

area.title: resources | gateways | nodes | pools | backups | alerts | selfha | tls | hygiene

subject.description: The resource, node or channel concerned; empty for an area-wide line.

status.description: pass | warn | fail | error ("error": the check itself could not run).

evidence.description: What was seen, one fact per entry.

fix.description: A command to run as written: `haify ...` or a shell line.

runbook.description: A runbook (haify_runbook / MCP prompt) covering the repair, when one fits.

areas.description: The areas that were inspected; empty means all.

checks.description: Sorted by area, most serious first. Empty in ListInspections.

total.description: Entries held in total, so the UI can say whether it is showing everything.

node.description: The node whose ring buffer this is — the active controller, whichever it is.

truncated.description: True when the buffer has wrapped, i.e. older lines have been discarded.

published.description:
Total published since the controller started. Compared against the oldest
id returned, this tells a client whether history has been discarded.

dropped.description: Events dropped because a subscriber could not keep up.

kinds.description:
kinds lists the message formats this controller can render, so a client
does not have to carry its own copy of the list and go stale.

pool.description: pool is the destination pool; it must exist on every diskful node.

command.description:
The exact command that produced these lines, so an operator can repeat it
by hand and see the same thing. A diagnosis nobody can reproduce is a
rumour.

truncated.description:
True when max_lines cut this short: what follows is the tail of the record,
not all of it. A count of what was dropped is deliberately not reported —
the collector reads the tail and never sees the rest, so any number here
would be invented.

v1NodeCollectorOutput.description: NodeCollectorOutput is one collector's reading on one node.

reachable.description:
False when the node could not be reached at all. Distinguished from a
collector that ran and failed: an unreachable node is itself the finding.

labels.description:
labels are arbitrary key=value tags on the node (e.g. rack=A, zone=east)
used by placement constraints like replicas_on_different.

replicationAddress.description:
replication_address is the address DRBD uses for this node. Empty means it
shares `address` (the historical single-network setup).

offlineSince.description:
offline_since is when the node stopped answering (Unix seconds), 0 while
it answers. Self-healing counts from it.

syncPercent.description:
Percent of this peer's data in sync (0..100). 100 when steady-state / not
resyncing. Only meaningful for a peer whose replication_state is a resync
state (SyncSource/SyncTarget/PausedSync*).

node.description:
node is the Haify node name this state belongs to. The map itself is keyed by
DRBD host name, which is the machine's real hostname and generally is NOT
the node name the rest of the API uses — so without this a caller cannot
pair a state with the entry of `nodes` it describes.

connection.description:
Peer DRBD connection state as the answering node sees it ("Connected",
"Connecting", "StandAlone", ...). Empty for the answering node itself. A
peer that is not Connected reports no role, disk or replication state, so
this is the only field that tells an unreachable replica from a healthy one.

tls.description: tls is whether the connection to this peer runs over TLS.

writtenKib.description:
KiB written to and read from the answering node's own DRBD device since
it came up there, summed over volumes. Set on the answering node's entry
only (the one with no replication_state); unset when DRBD did not report
them. Two readings over time give the resource's write and read rate.

sentKib.description:
KiB the answering node sent to and received from this peer since their
connection came up, summed over volumes. Set on peer entries only.

problem.description: problem says what stops the node from carrying an encrypted connection.

kind.description: kind is generic | feishu | slack | wecom | dingtalk.

v1NotifyChannelInfo.description:
NotifyChannelInfo describes one alert delivery channel. The signing secret is
intentionally absent, exactly as BackupTargetInfo omits its credential: a
secret readable back out of the API leaks through every client that renders
it. has_secret says whether one is stored, which is what a UI needs in order
to show "configured" without showing the value.

v1OcfAgent.description:
OcfAgent is one OCF resource-agent entry to compose into an HA promoter's
start[] list. It renders as "ocf:<provider>:<name> <instance> <k>=<v> ...".

apply.title: run the plan (one move at a time); otherwise only propose it

notes.title: what was left out, and why

health.description:
health is "ok", "warn", "fail" or "unknown" (no SMART on this device,
e.g. a virtual disk); health_detail says why.

cached.description:
Storage tiering (lvmcache). A pool with no fast tier reports cached=false
and leaves the rest zero, so a tiered pool is distinguishable from a plain
one in a plain `pool list`.

cacheSizeBytes.description: Size of the fast device given to the cache.

cacheUsedPercent.description:
Kernel dm-cache counters, rounded to whole percent. hit_percent is
cumulative since the cache was last activated, not a moving average.

cacheDirtyPercent.description:
Share of the cache holding writes that have not reached the slow device.
Zero on a writethrough cache by construction; on a writeback cache this is
the size of the window that a lost SSD would take with it.

cacheDevice.description: The fast block device backing the cache, as the node names it.

cacheDegraded.description:
True when LVM reports the cache as unhealthy — a cache in this state
cannot be flushed, so it cannot be detached without discarding data.

thinPoolLv.description:
Thin pool utilisation. total_gb/free_gb above describe the VOLUME GROUP,
and Haify gives its thin pool 95% of the group's free extents at create (all
of them on convert-thin), so free_gb stays near zero for the whole life of
such a pool however empty it is. These fields are the ones that say
whether the next write will succeed.

thin_pool_lv is empty when the group holds no thin pool; that — not a zero
percentage — is how "no thin pool" is told apart from "a thin pool at 0%".

thinSizeBytes.description: Capacity of the thin pool itself, which data_percent is a percentage of.

thinMetadataPercent.description:
Metadata exhaustion stops writes as completely as data exhaustion, and the
two fill for unrelated reasons, so neither substitutes for the other.

thinOutOfSpace.description:
LVM's own verdict, from the volume health field of lv_attr rather than
inferred from a percentage. A pool in this state has already refused
writes, and the kernel drops the backing disk out from under DRBD.

totalBytes.description:
Exact capacity. total_gb/free_gb are rounded to whole gibibytes and are
kept for compatibility; anything doing arithmetic or rendering a precise
size should use these.

compressRatio.description:
compress_ratio is how much compression saves on a ZFS pool, as ZFS
reports it (1.85 means 1.85x); 0 when not reported. compression above is
the algorithm in use.

hasVdo.description:
VDO-backed thin pools (type "thin_vdo"). thin_data_percent above is the
logical space handed out; vdo_physical_percent is the physical space
deduplication and compression did not save, and the one that, at 100%,
turns writes into I/O errors. has_vdo is false for any other pool.

capacityBytes.description:
What new volumes are carved from. On a pool with a thin pool in it that is
the thin pool: capacity_bytes is its size and available_bytes what its data
has not used. The volume group around it is nearly all allocated to it, so
total_*/free_* (which always describe the volume group or ZFS pool) read
near-full however empty the thin pool is. Elsewhere both equal
total_bytes/free_bytes. Zero when the controller could not measure them.

bytesCopied.description: bytes_copied is what dd reported, for logging and progress reporting.

v1ProfileMemberResult.description: ProfileMemberResult is what a profile operation did to one member resource.

members.description:
members is every node in the resource config: diskful replicas, diskless
tiebreakers and diskless clients alike. DRBD counts them all.

required.description: required is the majority DRBD needs to keep serving: members/2 + 1.

online.description:
online is how many members the reporting node can currently see, itself
included.

hasQuorum.description:
has_quorum is what DRBD itself reports, not a recomputation of the fields
above — they can disagree while a connection is being established, and DRBD
is the one that decides whether I/O proceeds.

tolerated.description:
tolerated is how many further members can be lost before I/O suspends.
Negative is not possible; zero means the next failure stops the resource.

v1QuorumInfo.description: QuorumInfo is the vote arithmetic behind "will this resource survive?".

replicationAddress.description:
replication_address is the address DRBD uses for this node in generated
.res files, letting replication traffic ride a dedicated NIC/subnet while
the controller keeps reaching the node over `address` (SSH/management).
Empty means "same as address", which is the historical behavior.

expectedLegs.description: Legs the resource should have, as "<node> -> <leg id>".

removedLegs.description: Instances removed (or, under dry_run, that would be), as "<host>: <leg id>".

disklessNodes.description: Nodes participating only as diskless quorum tiebreakers (vote, no data).

quorumRisk.description:
True when the resource has two diskful nodes and no tiebreaker, so a
single node failure suspends I/O (no quorum majority).

disklessClients.description:
Nodes attached as diskless data clients: no local replica, but connected
over DRBD and promotable to serve the volume over the network. Distinct
from diskless_nodes (quorum-only tiebreakers).

wanMode.description:
WAN replication: wan_mode marks a resource with an off-site asynchronous
copy, and dr_node names which of `nodes` holds it. Without this the list
shows the DR as just another replica, which is exactly wrong — it is a
different site, a different protocol, and it never takes over automatically.

encrypted.description:
encrypted is true when every replica's backing volume is a LUKS2 container
(DRBD → LUKS → LVM/ZFS). Encryption at rest only — DRBD replicates the
plaintext, so the wire is not protected by this.

faultDomainRisk.description:
fault_domain_risk names the labelled fault domain(s), e.g. "host=dell",
whose loss would take every copy of the data or the quorum majority.

wan.description:
WAN replication (all empty/false for an ordinary LAN resource). When wan is
true this resource replicates over the internet via a per-resource haify-proxy
pair (protocol A / async), so the DR peer can lag; wan_proxy reports each
WAN node's `haify-proxy@<resource>` unit state (active/inactive/...).

wanReachable.description:
wan_reachable is true when the primary node can currently open a TCP
connection to the DR WAN endpoint (i.e. the DR firewall/security group
permits the mTLS port). False here explains a WAN resource that is up
locally but not replicating.

wanMetrics.description:
wan_metrics carries the counters haify-proxy publishes on the primary. Absent
when they could not be read (older proxy, first tick not yet written, node
unreachable) — absent means UNKNOWN, not zero.

quorum.description:
quorum is what decides whether this resource keeps serving when nodes are
lost. It is the one number that governs availability and it was previously
reported nowhere: an operator had to know DRBD counts every configured node
(tiebreakers and the off-site DR included) and work out the majority by hand.

encrypted.description:
encrypted mirrors ResourceInfo.encrypted: the backing volumes are LUKS2
containers. Reported here because "is this volume encrypted?" is a question
an auditor asks of the running system, not of the creation request.

areas.description: Restrict to these areas; empty inspects everything.

path.description: Relative to the gateway's data volume; empty is the whole volume.

validUsers.description: Empty: every SMB user of the gateway.

secret.description:
secret is the signing secret for kinds that authenticate that way
(DingTalk's 加签). Write-only: never returned by any RPC.

An empty secret on an existing channel LEAVES THE STORED ONE ALONE, because
a UI cannot render the secret to send it back, so an edit of any other
field would otherwise silently clear it. clear_secret is how a secret is
actually removed.

v1SaveNotifyChannelRequest.description: SaveNotifyChannelRequest creates a channel or replaces one by name.

resources.description: resources whose DRBD config now carries the new address.

failed.description: failed names each resource that could not be rewritten, with the reason.

nodes.description: nodes to prepare; empty prepares every registered node.

frozen.title: false when the app was not running (nothing to freeze)

origin.description:
The logical volume this snapshot was taken from. A pool holds the snapshots
of every resource on its node, and the snapshot name alone does not say
which one it belongs to.

lockDays.description: lock_days locks every snapshot the schedule takes for that many days.

lockedUntil.description:
locked_until (RFC3339) is when the newest snapshot it took stops being
locked; until then the schedule and its resource cannot be deleted.

frozenUntil.description: frozen_until (RFC3339) is when a freeze ends; empty when not frozen.

message.description:
message carries the far end's own rejection text when it refused, which is
the part that says what to fix.

node.description: node limits the trim to one node; empty trims every online node.

state.description: state is "verifying", "done", or why the peer was skipped.

outOfSyncKib.description:
out_of_sync_kib is how much DRBD has marked out of sync with this peer in
all: what this verify found, plus whatever was marked before it. Marks
are set by verify and never cleared by it — only a resync clears them.

foundKib.description:
found_kib is the part of out_of_sync_kib this verify added. It is only
meaningful when baseline_known: a verify that is followed from another
call, or across a controller restart, has no record of what was marked
before it started.

pool.description: Storage pool (volume group) backing this volume.

backingVolume.description:
Backing logical volume name inside the pool (e.g. "<resource>_data").
Combined with pool it forms the "<pool>/<lv>" path used by snapshot APIs.

encrypted.description:
encrypted is true when DRBD consumes this volume through a LUKS2 container
rather than the backing LV/zvol directly. Snapshots of an encrypted volume
are snapshots of the ciphertext.

sizeBytes.description:
size_bytes is the device's exact size when it was given one; 0 means
size_gb whole GiB.

v1VolumeSpec.description:
VolumeSpec is one DRBD volume within a resource. storage_type comes from the
resource; each volume may target its own pool.

bufferUsedBytes.description:
buffer_used_bytes is the un-replicated backlog: writes the primary's DRBD
has already acknowledged to its application that have NOT yet reached the
DR site. Under protocol A this IS the data-loss window of a DR failover
performed right now — the question `resource status` previously could not
answer.

drbdToWanBytes.description:
Payload accepted from DRBD versus bytes actually put on the WAN, and the
ratio between them: the compression the link is really achieving.

reconnects.description:
reconnects climbing on an otherwise healthy link is the signature of a
flapping path; ring_full_events non-zero means the WAN could not keep up
with the write workload and DRBD was pushed into Ahead.

v1WANMetrics.description: WANMetrics is what the primary site's haify-proxy reports about the WAN leg.
